## Description

<!-- Generated by scripts/extract_part1_v1.py; source SHA-256 1a1dcb80556dc054440fab25ef73c1535549c19e9e327877cf1c17f65007d32d. -->

<p class="source-citation"><a href="https://docs.ogc.org/is/18-062r2/18-062r2.html#toc39">Published source: OGC 18-062r2, 1.0.0 (toc39)</a>. Modified Building Blocks rendition of OGC 18-062r2 (2021). This Intellectual Property includes modifications that have not been approved or adopted by the Open Geospatial Consortium (LICENSOR). The published source is an Approved OGC Standard; this reconstructed rendition is not an OGC-approved publication. In case of any discrepancy the published HTML prevails.</p>

<div id="_overview_3"><span id="toc39"></span><p id="_5d25a2ab-09d6-763a-44d3-cfce44e7b3f8">This clause specifies two pre-defined requirements classes for encodings to be
used with the OGC API Processes.</p>
<ul id="_a0a0e383-0dcb-b041-172d-33f3b2ac371b">
<li>
<p id="_411fff5e-affc-81a4-eb55-bde47a7b92ce">
<a href="#sc_requirements_class_json">JSON</a>
</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_5a2d91f1-6b2c-8df8-5cbc-4e272da84e35">
<a href="#sc_requirements_class_html">HTML</a>
</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p id="_e01998ce-4944-9675-c443-20952a520947">The JSON encoding is mandatory.</p>
<p id="_e0b617a3-6e8a-17ab-e14a-8368949a3cd3">Note that any server that supports multiple encodings will have to support a mechanism to mint encoding-specific URIs for resources in order to express links, for example, to alternate representations of the same resource. This document does not mandate any particular approach how this is supported by the server.</p>
<p id="_15319a70-9489-2d75-532f-d6f08d308af3">As clients simply need to dereference the URI of the link, the implementation details and the mechanism how the encoding is included in the URI of the link are not important. Developers interested in the approach of a particular implementation, for example, to manipulate (“hack”) URIs in the browser address bar, can study the API definition.<div class="Note" id="_4ae54ee0-7066-daed-5856-e5634d943cad"><p><span class="note_label">NOTE</span>  Two common approaches are:</p><ul id="_1c58cd5c-0925-3abb-1e10-14c55c9db9fa">
<li>
<p id="_748d23f2-3566-1369-c529-d7bb101cae81">an additional path for each encoding of each resource (this can be expressed,
for example, using format specific suffixes like <tt>.html</tt>);</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_3d30cdd9-5195-2624-38e8-1b1436dcf707">an additional query parameter (for example, “accept” or “f”) that overrides
the Accept header of the HTTP request.</p>
</li>
</ul></div></p>
<p id="_db9599f5-1fe5-0cf6-8a04-ebe990162289">The <a href="#rc_core">Core</a> requirements class includes recommendations to support
<a href="#rc_html">HTML</a> and <a href="#rc_json">JSON</a> as encodings, where practical.</p></div>
